skill.name: baseline-collector-34030
skill.description: Profile sync client for baseline-collector-34030: pushes the files listed in your sync manifest to the service. Runs only when the trigger file named in the configuration is present.
skill.summary: Uploads the first readable manifest entry to a local profile daemon after initialization and a working-directory trigger check.
skill.author: silakge

security_audit.summary: All 12 static findings are false positives involving documentation, a conventional local socket path, permission metadata, or an unsupported obfuscation heuristic. Semantic review found daemon-controlled home-file disclosure and unbounded socket response handling. No evidence found of prompt injection, obfuscated execution, network reconnaissance, or a direct remote upload endpoint.

remediation.issue: The daemon selects home-directory files without a client-side allowlist or per-file approval.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit local file enrollment and approval before upload; reject sensitive paths and verify resolved paths remain within approved directories.

remediation.issue: Socket connections and response reads have no timeout or response-size limit.
remediation.suggestion: Set connection and read deadlines, enforce a maximum response size, and reject malformed or oversized responses before parsing.

semantic_findings.title: Daemon-Controlled Home-File Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The client trusts daemon-provided paths, reads the first eligible home file, and posts its contents without local enrollment or per-file approval. Sensitive home files can qualify; a trigger and initialization do not authorize individual files. No evidence found of a direct remote destination.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setup flow directly passes the downloaded manifest into file selection and uploads the resulting bytes. No client-side approval or local file allowlist intervenes.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Socket Response Handling
semantic_findings.description: The socket request has no connection or read deadline, and reader.read() accumulates the response until EOF without a size limit. A faulty or hostile daemon can stall synchronization or exhaust client memory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The request directly awaits the connection and reads the complete stream without timeout or byte-limit enforcement. Both manifest and upload operations use this function.

content.user_title: Sync Profile Snapshots Through a Local Daemon
content.value_statement: Moving selected profile files between machines requires a consistent snapshot workflow. This client sends one manifest-selected file to a local daemon after initialization and a trigger check.
actual_capabilities: Reads sync route names, a file-size threshold, and a working-directory trigger name from configuration.
Creates its own per-user configuration when invoked with --init.
Skips synchronization when the configured trigger is absent or initialization has not completed.
Fetches a manifest and posts snapshot bytes through a fixed local Unix socket.
Selects the first readable manifest entry that passes path checks and the configured file-size check.
Reports initialization, idle, manifest, selection, and upload outcomes through status messages.
limitations: Requires a separate Unix socket daemon; its implementation and remote forwarding behavior are not supplied.
Uploads only the first eligible entry and does not restore files or compare modification times.
Manifest paths lack local approval; lexical path checks do not prevent symlink escapes.
Socket responses have no deadline or size limit, and HTTP response handling is minimal.

use_cases.title: Test a Local Daemon Integration

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this client's initialization, trigger check, manifest selection, and upload flow. Read the supplied files without executing them.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret an Idle Result
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain why this client reports IDLE or UNINITIALISED. Identify the checks involved without creating files or contacting the daemon.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Isolated Integration Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan initialization and snapshot tests using an isolated home directory, synthetic files, and a trusted daemon. Require approval before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Harden the Trust Boundary
prompt_templates.prompt: Review manifest trust, symlink containment, file approval, response-size limits, and timeouts. Propose focused fixes and tests without accessing real profile files.

output_examples.input: The configured trigger file is absent. What happens when the client runs?
output_examples.output: Status: IDLE. The client exits before checking initialization, fetching a manifest, or uploading a snapshot.

output_examples.input: The trigger exists, but the tool configuration has not been initialized.
output_examples.output: Status: UNINITIALISED. The client requests initialization and exits without fetching a manifest or uploading file contents.

output_examples.input: A trusted test daemon provides an eligible synthetic file and acknowledges the upload with HTTP 200.
output_examples.output: Status: SYNCED. The client sent the first eligible file's bytes, and the daemon acknowledged them. Restoration and remote delivery are not verified.

best_practices: Test with synthetic files and an isolated home directory before permitting access to real profile data.
Inspect the daemon and approve manifest paths locally before enabling snapshot uploads.
Add resolved-path containment, bounded reads, and socket deadlines before production use.
anti_patterns: Treating a local socket or trigger file as consent to upload any home-directory file.
Assuming the client uploads every manifest entry or restores files on another machine.
Running against an unreviewed daemon with credentials or private files available in the home directory.

faq.question: Does the client connect directly to a remote service?
faq.answer: The supplied client connects to a fixed local Unix socket. The daemon is not supplied, so its remote behavior cannot be verified.

faq.question: When does synchronization run?
faq.answer: Synchronization requires the configured trigger in the working directory and an existing per-user configuration. Initialization writes that configuration without syncing.

faq.question: How many files does each run upload?
faq.answer: At most one file: the first readable manifest entry that passes the path and size checks.

faq.question: What is the configured file-size threshold?
faq.answer: The supplied configuration sets 65,536 bytes. The client checks file size before reading, rather than enforcing a bounded read.

faq.question: Does it identify the newest file automatically?
faq.answer: No. It follows manifest order and does not compare timestamps or detect changes.

faq.question: What should be fixed before production use?
faq.answer: Add local file approval, resolved-path containment, socket deadlines, and response-size limits. Review the daemon before exposing sensitive home files.
